courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Religion and Racism
courses.description: How does religion become a source of ethnic or racial prejudice among religious practitioners? When does prejudice against religious persons constitute a form of racism? This class explores answers to these questions by examining the connections between religion and racism in modern societies like the United States and South Africa.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Religion, Magic, and Science
courses.description: This course explores the ways in which religion, magic, and science are defined in the modern world and the different forms in which supernaturalism circulates within contemporary culture.

source.text: RELI 61. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: A History of Heresy: Christian Dissent from the Gnostics to the Pentecostals
courses.description: Christian orthodox beliefs or practices often get formulated expressly to marginalize a viewpoint or community considered too radical. This course examines a variety of Western Christian dissenters and the authorities who opposed them: Gnostics; medieval, Spanish, and Latin American inquisitions; Protestant Anabaptists; witches; Galileo; Mormons; and Pentecostals.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Archaeology of Qumran and the Dead Sea Scrolls
courses.description: In this seminar students learn about the Dead Sea Scrolls, ancient manuscripts dating to the time of Jesus from caves around the site of Qumran by the Dead Sea. They include early copies of the Hebrew Bible (Old Testament) and sectarian works belonging to the Jewish community that lived in Qumran.

source.text: RELI 63. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Reintroducing Islam
courses.description: An introduction to the Islamic religious tradition, focusing on major themes of Islamic religious thought, bringing out both traditional spirituality and the critical issues confronting Muslims today.

source.text: RELI 64. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-GLOBAL or FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Myth, Philosophy, and Science in the Ancient World
courses.description: This course examines the conflicting ways in which ancient myth, science, and philosophy explained creation of the universe, origins of mankind, nature of dreams, and foundations of culture.

source.text: RELI 65. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Buddhism in America: From the Buddha to the Beastie Boys
courses.description: Introduces students to Buddhism and traces its history in the United States, highlighting the period since 1965. It focuses on immigrants, converts, and the cultural influence of Buddhism in America.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Personhood, Identity and the Individual: How Religion Shapes Social Life
courses.description: What is a person and how do we know this? This course investigates how different religious and cultural communities conceptualize human nature and the implications of these understandings for the ways we understand ourselves and organize public life. Readings include case studies from places including India, Nepal, and the United States. Students will also undertake a hands-on research project. The Honors version includes additional readings on economic personhood and assignments that ask students to analyze expressive performances in ways that draw on and extend learning goals from the course. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 67. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: FYS: Charisma in Religion, Science, and Poetry Studies in the Entrepreneurial Imagination
courses.description: A comparative examination of prophet, scientist, and poet as critics and creators of the entrepreneurial outlook and sensibility in individuals and organizations with special attention to innovator's dilemmas. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Gender and Sexuality in Contemporary Judaism
courses.description: Taking a global perspective, the course compares the manners in which Jewish communities in America, Israel, Europe, Asia, and Africa have accommodated themselves to the changing norms in gender and sexuality in the last generation.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Jesus in Scholarship and Film
courses.description: This seminar explores the ways the historical Jesus has been portrayed in the writings of modern scholars and films of the 20th and 21st centuries.

source.text: RELI 70. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Spirit of Capitalism
courses.description: Examines scholarly work on the overlap of religion and capitalism.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Apocalypse Now? Messianic Movements in America
courses.description: This course explores the messianic idea in America as well as the messianic movements that have been active in the nation's history and their interaction with American society and culture.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: From Dragons to Pokemon: Animals in Japanese Myth, Folklore, and Religion
courses.description: This course examines the cultural construction of animals in Japanese myth, folklore, and religion. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Person, Time, and Religious Conduct
courses.description: Within the vast field of activity called "religion," this course examines how people and societies give meaning to the relation between human organisms and the universe in time and space. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Sacrifice and Surrender
courses.description: This course will consider the questions of debt, loss, and surrender as we explore the problem of sacrifice. Readings will address the associated problems of violence, transgression, and animality.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Money and Morality: Divining Value in Social Life
courses.description: This seminar explores the many ways that different religions and cultures have imagined spiritual wealth, secular riches, and the appropriate modes of interaction between them in different places and times.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Martyrs and Warriors: Religion and the Problem of Violence
courses.description: This seminar asks why some people choose to take life (their own or another's) for religious purposes and how texts, practices, and communities shape these motives. Focuses on martyrological traditions in Western religions, but also tracks idioms of war, sacrifice, and ritualized suffering in other religious contexts and secular discourses.

source.text: RELI 77. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-GLOBAL or FC-VALUES.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Reading the Bible: Now and Then
courses.description: An introduction to the interpretation of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament. We will look at the biblical text as modern interpreters and through the eyes of the Bible's earliest Jewish and Christian interpreters with special attention to changing assumptions about how to read the Bible and the nature of Scripture itself.

source.text: RELI 78. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Human Animals in Religion and Ethics
courses.description: This course investigates the figure of the human animal in religion and philosophy. What kind of animal is the human, and what separates humans from animals? We will consider how attending to distinctions between humans and animals can highlight varying ideological and religious viewpoints.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Religion and Writing in the Ancient World
courses.description: This seminar considers the role of writing as a technology in the shaping of ancient religious traditions, from the inventions of writing in Mesopotamia and Egypt to the advent of Islam. Topics include the early alphabet, magical/mystical uses of writing, religion and literacy, and the development of "Scripture" (e.g., Bible, Qur'an).

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Sex, Marriage, and Family in Religion
courses.description: This course approaches the central role of discourses about sexual norms, marriage, and family in select religious traditions. It asks how religious traditions have defined and negotiated normative models for marriage and family in their connection to larger theological frameworks and religious source texts.

source.text: RELI 85. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-POWER or FC-VALUES.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Confessions
courses.description: This course will examine autobiographies and memoirs from at least two religious traditions and different historical eras, in which individuals interpret their changing religious identity through first-person narrative and/or artistic expression. We will consider how individuals negotiate and represent themselves to different communities according to need, time, and circumstance.

source.text: RELI 87. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Religion and Society in Historical Novels
courses.description: In this seminar we will read several books. Most of them are bestsellers and can be described as "historical novels." Having these books as a starting point, we will explore religion and society in Europe and the Middle East in the medieval and early modern period.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to Religious Studies
courses.description: An introduction to the academic study of religion that considers approaches to the interpretation of religion and includes study of several religious traditions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: World Religions
courses.description: This course examines forms of religious expression as embodied in several important religious traditions. It investigates religious experience; myth and ritual; teachings and scripture; historical, social, and artistic aspects of religion; and the nature and function of religion in society, with a special focus on ethics and values.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Understanding the Bible: Hebrew Bible/Old Testament
courses.description: This course teaches students how to understand the various books of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament in light of the history and culture of the ancient Israelites responsible for producing them. It asks students to compare the values with which they today approach reading the Bible with the work these texts would have performed in their ancient context. Among other topics, it addresses how the past is used for the formation of national identity, how divinity is conceptualized, ancient forms of worship and social and ethical values, and how biblical texts were used within early Judaism and Christianity. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 103. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | JWST 103 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Understanding the Bible: The New Testament and Christian Literature
courses.description: This course studies the New Testament from both a literary and a historical perspective, focusing on its origins in the land of Israel and moving into the eastern Mediterranean. In it students learn to wrestle with the nature of historical evidence, develop their skills for making argumentation, and learn how to analyze the philosophical and ethical claims of the ancient Christian texts, and participate in class debates on contemporary ethical issues. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religions of the Greco-Roman World
courses.description: An introduction to religions and the religious life of the ancient world (1000 BCE-300 CE) in various cultural settings: Greek cities, cosmopolitan Hellenistic kingdoms in Egypt and Syria, and the Roman Empire.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Judaism in the Time of Jesus
courses.description: This course surveys Jewish history and religion during the Second Temple and Rabbinic periods, from the destruction of the First Jewish Temple (Solomon's Temple) in 586 BCE to the Muslim conquest of Palestine (640 CE).

source.text: RELI 106. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES. | JWST 106 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to Modern Judaism
courses.description: The course offers a comprehensive understanding of the development of Judaism from the late Middle Ages to contemporary times.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Classic Jewish Texts: From Bible and Dead Sea Scrolls to Kabbalah and Hassidism
courses.description: This course will explore Jewish literary works that are considered "fundamental," "classic," "traditional" (often, all of the above), including the Hebrew Bible, the Mishnah, the Babylonian Talmud, midrashic collections, works by Maimonides, major codes of Jewish law, major kabbalistic, philosophic, poetic, and ethical works, hassidic compositions, and more.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: History and Culture of Ancient Israel
courses.description: An examination extending from Hebrew origins to the Babylonian exile and including political history as well as social and religious institutions. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Archaeology of Palestine in the New Testament Period
courses.description: This course surveys the archaeology of Palestine (modern Israel and Jordan) from the Persian period (ca. 586 BCE) to the Muslim conquest (640 CE).

source.text: RELI 110. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST. | CLAR 110 , JWST 110 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Abrahamic Religions
courses.description: This course addresses the history, texts, rituals, festivals, and ethics of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam in a global context.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: A Global History of the Bible
courses.description: This course examines the global history of the Bible. What the Bible is -- the Bible's identity -- is determined by how it has been used within the multitude of communities that have engaged it across the globe for over two millennia. The course begins with the Bible's earliest origins in the ancient Near East, explores its role in the formation of Judaism and Christianity, traces its spread throughout the globe through translation and missionary activity, considers its transformations in the modern period, and concludes with its varied uses in the contemporary world.

source.text: RELI 112. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL. | JWST 112 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Early Christian Worship, Ritual, and Bodies
courses.description: What did the earliest Christian churches look like? How did Christians worship, and what behaviors and gestures set them apart from other ancient communities? This course probes these questions, illustrating how different Christian groups developed different ways of regulating the body, food, space, and gender, and how this diversity still impacts contemporary global Christian cultures. Topics include the evolution of baptism, exorcism, marriage, speaking in tongues, and burial rites. Previously offered as RELI 214.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Culture of the Ancient Near East
courses.description: An overview of the history and culture of the ancient Near East, from the birth of writing through the first millennium BCE, covering the regions of Mesopotamia, Egypt, Anatolia, and Syria-Palestine.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to Religion and Culture
courses.description: An introductory course that explores relations between religion and culture through the examination of social theory and the analysis of case studies. The case studies focus on such issues as visual culture, ritual, media, gender, and politics. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophical Approaches to Religion
courses.description: An introduction to philosophical approaches to the study of religion, exploring such topics as religious language and experience, the problem of evil, the relation between religious belief and practice, and issues of religious diversity. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to Jewish Studies
courses.description: This course introduces students to the field of Jewish studies as an academic discipline. Jewish studies is by nature interdisciplinary and can be approached from a variety of viewpoints and discourses. The course will address foundational texts, developments, and ideas in Judaism from the biblical world to contemporary contexts, while exploring major approaches to Jewish studies in the scholarly world today.

source.text: RELI 123I. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES, INTERDISCI. | JWST 100I .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Heaven and Hell
courses.description: This course will explore cultural development and significance of religious notions of an afterlife. Are they coherent? What alternative notions of life after death can we imagine?

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Reason, Faith, and God: Philosophy of Western Religion
courses.description: A philosophical inquiry into the problems of religious experience and belief, as expressed in philosophic, religious, and literary documents from traditional and contemporary sources. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 126. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | PHIL 134 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Claims of Science and Religion
courses.description: This course explores the sometimes competing, sometimes compatible claims of science and religion, including conflicting views about creation, miracles, rituals, revelation, and human nature. Global and historical case studies will enable students to consider claims to authority (religious, philosophical, medical, and scientific), types of proof, and ethical implications.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Popular Culture
courses.description: Examines representations of religion in mass media, as well as the interplay of religious ideas and popular cultures.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Global Justice
courses.description: In this course, students review the intersections of religious thought and social justice around the globe. We will review how liberation theologies emerge, for example, as pathways for addressing various social issues related to food insecurity, reproductive health, migration and citizenship, race, poverty, and religious freedom. Students will explore various debates related to ethics and social justice in relation to the study of religion in multiple geographic contexts.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to Religious Ethics
courses.description: A study of the nature, methods, and aims of ethics as seen in exemplary persons and actions with emphasis on religious and social context and contemporary problems. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion, Ethics, and Technology
courses.description: This course examines the ethical quandaries that emerge as new technologies are mobilized in religious cultures. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religious Freedom
courses.description: This course explores the development of religious liberty and freedom of conscience in Western culture by examining both the historical emergence of these concepts and important contemporary controversies.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in America
courses.description: An introduction to the history, themes, and issues in American religion from the precolonial period to the present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: African American Religions
courses.description: Survey of the historical development of various African American religious traditions, with emphasis on folk spirituality, gender issues, black nationalism, and the role of the church in the black community. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Catholicism in America
courses.description: An introduction to Roman Catholicism in the United States.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Judaism in Our Time
courses.description: An examination of Judaism in its two major centers, demonstrating how different social and cultural environments shape very different interpretations and practices of the Jewish tradition.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Indigenous Religion in the Americas
courses.description: This course explores Indigenous religions in the Americas. It employs both historical survey and ethnographic methods to introduce diverse beliefs, practices, materials, and locations cultivated by Native American communities. Far from recognizing any boundary between the sacred and profane, it surveys Indigenous approaches gender, spirituality, cosmology, rituals, healing, sickness, human rights, and language, with a particular focus on Nahuatl. Nahuatl or Aztec language is the Indigenous language most spoken in Mexico after Spanish. Studies will also interrogate long legacies of contact with Indigenous communities and European religions in the context of conquest, colonization, revolt, and revitalization.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in Latin America
courses.description: This course surveys the history of Latin American religious traditions from precontact to the present. It explores the contributions of African, indigenous, and European traditions as well as the extraordinary combinations that resulted from their interaction.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Indigenous Well-Being
courses.description: The course explores several Indigenous populations from Latin America including Mexico and Guatemala. The course begins with historical studies of Indigenous people, examining topics such as colonization and cultural trauma experienced after the conquest of Mexico in the Sixteenth Century until today. The course analyzes the relations among religion, ritual practices, sacred landscapes, health, diseases, addictions, gender, discrimination, human rights, and economic inequalities, experienced among Indigenous peoples in the Americas. Students will also learn about cultural wealth preserved by the Indigenous cultures and its contributions to the global world to obtain well-being.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to the History of Christian Traditions
courses.description: Analysis of continuities and innovations in the history of Christian traditions in the West and globally. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Catholicism Today: An Introduction to the Contemporary Catholic Church
courses.description: This course provides students with a first glimpse and insight into the Catholic tradition, past, present, and future: its beliefs, structure, aims, successes, and failures.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Critical Issues in Western Religious Thought
courses.description: A consideration of major questions concerning religion in modern culture.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Heresy and Inquisition: Religion, Ethics, Marginalization
courses.description: During the Middle Ages and the early modern era, various inquisitions used legal inquiry and torture to determine the boundaries of heresy. This course surveys the influence of these regimes on the doctrine, practices, and morality of heretics, mystics, witches, Jews, and Muslims, in the interest of delimiting "orthodox" Catholicism.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Mysticism
courses.description: Comparative study of mysticism in several religious traditions, Eastern and Western. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ideals, Cultures, and Rituals of the University
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A religious studies approach to the rituals, cultures, and disciplines of the university, assessing the ways in which explanatory ideals are embedded, changed, and promoted. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Global Christianity
courses.description: Christianity began in Asia and Africa, followed by expansion into Europe and eventually the Americas. Now, the Global South again has the highest population of Christians. This course examines the geographical expansion of Christianity in its early history, then turns to modern and current processes of enculturation and globalization as well as inter-religious dynamics.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islam and Muslim Life before 1500
courses.description: A broad and comprehensive introduction to Islam from its beginnings to the end of the 15th century, with a focus on Muslim experiences, discourses, and practices. Students may not receive credit for both RELI 180 / ASIA 180 and ASIA 138 / HIST 138 .

source.text: RELI 180. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST. | ASIA 180 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islam and Muslim Life since 1500
courses.description: A broad and comprehensive introduction to Islam and important developments in Muslim experiences, discourses, and practices since the 16th century and up to the present. Topics include Muslim experiences with modernity, colonialism, and nationalism, Muslim reform movements and social justice activism, and shifts in Qur'an interpretation, Islamic law, and religious practice. Students may not receive credit for both RELI 181 / ASIA 181 and ASIA 139 / HIST 139 .

source.text: RELI 181. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | ASIA 181 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Asian Religions
courses.description: An introduction to major religions of South Asia and East Asia, such as Hinduism, Sikhism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Daoism, and Shinto.

source.text: RELI 183. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-KNOWING. | ASIA 183 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: East Asian Religions
courses.description: This course surveys East Asian religions and their relationship with the natural world. It provides an East Asian religious perspective on environmental thought and an environmental perspective on East Asian religions. We will explore parallels and divergences, and how each can enrich and critique the other.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Women/Gender/Islam
courses.description: A survey of gender roles in Muslim societies from the advent of Islam to the present. It explores how Muslims have interpreted the Qur'an to determine discourses on gender and sexuality and emphasizes the role of religious authority as well as historical/geographical contexts for Muslim women's lives. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Subject matter will vary with instructor but will always be focused on a particular problem or issue.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Special Topics in Religious Studies, FC-VALUES
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ancient Biblical Interpretation
courses.description: The course looks at the origins of biblical interpretation, how the Hebrew Bible was interpreted around the turn of the Common Era, the key formative period for early Christianity and rabbinic Judaism. We consider the nature of interpretation as an endeavor, as well as how the Bible came to be viewed as Scripture. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Sacrifice in the Ancient World
courses.description: This course examines the religious phenomenon of sacrifice with a focus on examples from the ancient Mediterranean world (including Greece, ancient Israel, and the Near East). Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Prophecy and Divination in Ancient Israel and Judah
courses.description: An examination of prophecy and divination in the Israelite-Jewish traditions and in their environments, including an analysis of the major biblical prophets. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Jesus in the Early Christian Gospels
courses.description: An analysis of the variety of traditions used in the first two centuries to portray Jesus, focusing on the reasons for this variety and the historical and literary problems it presents.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Birth of Christianity
courses.description: An analysis of the origin of the Christian church and its early expansion, with particular emphasis on the problems evident in the shift from a Jewish to a Gentile framework. Paul's role in defining and resolving the issues is considered in detail and evaluated in the light of subsequent events.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Varieties of Early Christianity
courses.description: A study of various forms of Christianity in the second and third centuries (e.g., Gnosticism, Marcionism, Montanism), focusing on their polemical relationship to orthodox Christianity. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Classical Hebrew I: A Linguistic Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
courses.description: An introduction to the culture and history of ancient Israel through an exploration of the language of the Hebrew Bible. Students will learn the essentials for basic engagement with biblical Hebrew, then consider what this linguistic evidence reveals about the historical and cultural background of the Hebrew Bible.

source.text: RELI 211. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST. | JWST 211 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Classical Hebrew II: A Linguistic Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
courses.description: This course explores the linguistic background of the Hebrew Bible, giving special attention to the literary aspect of biblical interpretation. Specific topics include the forms of the Hebrew verb, prose and poetic genres in the Hebrew Bible, wordplay and repetition, narration and dialogue.

source.text: RELI 212. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, RELI 211 . | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | JWST 212 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Eastern Christian Cultures: Middle East, Asia, Africa, and Eastern Europe
courses.description: Although Christianity is characteristically identified with "the West", the Middle East, Asia, and Africa have been home to native Christian populations for 2,000 years. This course surveys the diversity of these 300 million "Eastern" and/or "Orthodox" Christians, often marginalized in surveys of global Christianity. It highlights how these communities articulate their identities around particular linguistic, ritual, and cultural markers, and the struggle they face preserving these identities in the West following refugee and migrant experiences.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Gnosticism
courses.description: A comprehensive survey of ancient Christian Gnosticism, one of the earliest and most long-lived branches of early Christianity, with principal readings drawn from the famous "Nag Hammadi Library." Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Christianity and Islam in the Middle Ages
courses.description: This course draws on a variety of cultural documents to explore both the conflict and cross fertilization between the Christian and Islamic cultures of the Middle Ages. Readings and discussions in English. Previously offered as GERM 218.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Medicine
courses.description: This course will deal with global interactions of religion, health care, medical ethics, disability, and the body in the past and present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Modern Western Religious Thought
courses.description: Representative themes and approaches in the work of modern Western religious thinkers.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Modern Jewish Thought
courses.description: This course examines how contemporary thinkers have considered philosophy, ethics, and theology from a Jewish perspective. Methodological points of inquiry include: the role of interpretation in Judaism, revelation and redemption, authority and tradition, pluralism and inclusion, suffering and evil, gender and Jewish philosophy, and 20th-century approaches to God. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 224. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | JWST 224 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Christian Cultures
courses.description: This course explores the range of cultural manifestations of Christianity in the contemporary world, focusing particularly on differences of race, ethnicity, gender, geography, and class.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Human Animals in Religion and Ethics
courses.description: This course investigates the figure of the human animal in religion and philosophy. What kind of animal is the human, and what separates humans from animals? We will consider how attending to distinctions between humans and animals can highlight varying ideological and religious viewpoints.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Luther and the Bible
courses.description: The Reformation was seminal for the development of the modern world. This course will investigate Reformation literature written in the period from the end of the 15th century to the end of the 17th century, and will investigate how Reformation ideas resonate through today. Readings and discussions in English.

source.text: RELI 227. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST. | GERM 227 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Judaism and Popular Culture
courses.description: This course explores connections and interactions between Judaism and popular culture in the American context. We will consider what counts as religion by examining and interpreting a series of contemporary case studies drawn from film, television, radio, consumer culture, literature, stand-up comedy, and other media.

source.text: RELI 230. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | JWST 230 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Bible in America
courses.description: This course explores the pervasive role that the Bible has occupied in America's culture and institutions from the time of the Founding Fathers to the present day.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Shrines and Pilgrimages
courses.description: An introduction to the study of shrines and pilgrimage in multiple cultural contexts.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Violence
courses.description: This course examines the problematic interplay between religion and violence. It engages and tests accusations that religion is inherently violent through the reading of sacred texts, historical cases, and critical theories.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Place, Space, and Religion
courses.description: A consideration of the attitudes toward place and space as they are expressed in religious ritual and artifact.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religious Things
courses.description: An introduction to religion and visual culture in the United States. The course focuses on painting, ritual objects, and architecture.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Bible and its Others
courses.description: This course asks students to interrogate the ways in which the Bible relates to its others, those who are on the margins of society, whether because of ethnicity, gender, class, or other features. It asks how relating to this "other" can become a way of forging group identity, in what ways that occurs at the expense of the wellbeing of the marginalized, and what efforts are made to protect them. The course will examine these questions not only from the perspective of the biblical text but from the full global history of the Bible in different time periods and geographies. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: German Culture and the Jewish Question
courses.description: A study of the role of Jews and the "Jewish question" in German culture from 1750 to the Holocaust and beyond. Discussions and texts (literary, political, theological) in English. Previously offered as GERM 270.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion, Literature, and the Arts in America
courses.description: Engages literary, performing, and visual arts to explore religion in American culture. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Messianic Movements in American History
courses.description: The course examines messianic movements in American history raising the questions, What has been the impact of such movements on the nation? What makes America particularly conducive to such movements?

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: New Religious Movements in America
courses.description: An introduction to new religious movements in the United States, with emphasis on the nature of conversion and the role of founders.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to American Judaism
courses.description: Course provides a comprehensive introduction to American Judaism, its various movements, institutions, theological, and liturgical characteristics, as well as its standing within the larger framework of religious life in America.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Western Christianity
courses.description: An examination of the development of teachings on issues of gender and sexuality through the history of Western Christianity, with particular focus on contemporary controversies. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 244. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | WGST 244 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Latina/o Religions in the United States-Mexico Borderlands
courses.description: The goal of this course is to orient students in the great diversity of Latina and Latino religious formations in the United States today. Focusing on Indigenous, African, and Catholic Creole "inspirations," this course will focus students to the emergence of a distinctly U.S. Latina/o religious experience. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Supernatural Encounters: Zombies, Vampires, Demons, and the Occult in the Americas
courses.description: This course examines accounts of supernatural beings such as zombies and vampires and aims to understand them as popular ways of making sense of the world in the context of uneven and frequently unsettling processes of modernization, neoliberalism, and globalization. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Uncertain Truths: Conspiracy Theories, Aliens, and Secret Societies in America
courses.description: This course examines the social dynamics of power, secrecy, paranoia, and suspicion, in order to explore the multiple relations between conspiracism, religious/magical thinking, and the social construction of truth. In addition to investigating the social and historical contexts that give rise to conspiracy thinking and the various shapes conspiracism takes in the modern world, students will consider conspiratorial lore as an important mode of political participation and contestation.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Introduction to American Islam
courses.description: This course surveys Muslim communities in North America in their religious, historical, political, social, and cultural dimensions. Discussion frames include methods for the study of American Muslims, the role of public and media representations of Islam and Muslims, and the place of American Muslims within the larger American religious landscape. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in Colonial Mexico
courses.description: The course will begin with historical studies of Nahuatl populations, examining history about the conquest of Mexico to better understand the impact of the arrival of Europeans and colonization. The course will then explore the diversity of Nahua culture in colonial Mexico and their production of indigenous knowledge. Topics include the Mesoamerican writing system, language, religion, gender, food, and literature production involving theater, poetry, and art production related to music of Nahua people. Students will learn about the cultural wealth preserved by the Nahuas indigenous culture and its contributions to the global world.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Christ's Passion Plays in Mexico
courses.description: This course explores the Christ's Passion Plays written and performed by Indigenous people in Colonial Mexico. After 1519 when Spaniards and friers came in Mexico, they also brought with them the Christian doctrine. Friers spread out Christianity in colonial Mexico and one of the methods to teach Christianity to Indigenous populations was through the theatrical evangelization. In the eighteenth century, Indigenous performances were prohibited by the Inquisition. In the twentieth century Indigenous performances appeared again in some neighborhoods in Mexico City and the most performed was the Christ's Passion and the Last Supper performed for the Holy week.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Gender and Religion in Premodern Europe
courses.description: This course examines gender in the religious lives of premodern Europeans from 500-1700, both in daily life (marriage, sexuality, devotions) and among the religious elite (clergy, monks and nuns, mystics). Feminist history, masculinity studies, and sexuality studies will all be taught as historical methods, paired with primary source documents from medieval Christians. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 263. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 263 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Medieval and Renaissance Christian Cultures
courses.description: This course explores the cultural manifestations of Christianity in the medieval and Renaissance worlds, focusing particularly on interactions with other religions and on differences of gender, geography, and class.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in Western Europe
courses.description: In this course, we will explore various topics related to the past and present status of religion in general, and of certain religions in particular, within three Western European countries: the United Kingdom, France, and Germany. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islamic Law, Ethics, and Practice
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to Islamic law in its connection to religious ethics and diverse ritual practices, both in the premodern and modern periods, and through an analysis of local contexts and global flows of ideas and practices that determine what is considered "Islamic" about laws, ethics, and practices.

source.text: RELI 279. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-KNOWING. | ASIA 279 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Hindu Gods and Goddesses
courses.description: This course focuses on how Hindu gods and goddesses are experienced in South Asia through analysis of literature and art, including texts, visual representations, film, comic books, performance, and ethnography. We will also examine key Hindu concepts (dharma, karma, and caste) in Hindu religious narratives. A key component of the course is oral communication. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Hinduism in the Americas
courses.description: This course introduces students to the diverse religious phenomena known as Hindu traditions as they manifest in the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. Approaching Hinduism as both a religion of immigrants and a tradition adopted and practiced by non-Indian Americans, it examines how Hindu practices have been embraced and transformed in North America and the local and global forces that affect this. Using case studies, we will explore the role of religion in fostering community identity, and the emergence of new theological and philosophical interpretations that respond to the unique challenges of diaspora.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Buddhist Tradition: India, Nepal, and Tibet
courses.description: Examines the diverse beliefs, practices, and cultures associated with Buddhism in the Himalayan regions of India, Nepal, and Tibet. Topics include Buddhism's development and spread, the cultural dynamics of Himalayan societies, monasticism, folk religion, revivalism, tourism, gender, globalization, and the role of the state in shaping Buddhist life and culture.

source.text: RELI 283. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | ASIA 300 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Buddhist Tradition: East Asia
courses.description: An examination of the development of Buddhism after its importation to East Asia.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Monks, Magic, & Meditation: Theravada Buddhism Across Space and Time
courses.description: This course explores the Theravada school of Buddhism: its ethical and philosophical teachings, social and civic norms it has chartered in Southeast Asia and Sri Lanka, and the forms and networks it has taken over time and across the globe focusing on the key tropes of monks, magic and meditation.

source.text: RELI 285. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | ASIA 285 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Premodern Japanese Religions
courses.description: This course surveys Shinto, Buddhism, Shugendo, and Christianity in premodern Japan, tracing their development from early kami worship through the early modern period. Students will examine themes such as the relationship between religion and the state, gender, material and visual culture, and cross-cultural exchange through historical texts, visual narratives, and ritual practices. Creative projects reimagine religious traditions and sacred spaces, using artistic expression alongside cultural and historical analysis to illuminate the role of religion in premodern Japanese society.

source.text: RELI 286. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | ASIA 286 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Modern Japanese Religions
courses.description: This course surveys Shinto, Buddhism, Christianity, and the New Religions in modern and contemporary Japan, tracing their transformations from the Meiji period to the present. Students will examine themes such as nationalism, gender, popular culture, and everyday practice through historical texts, ethnographies, and visual media. Creative projects reimagine religious practices and narratives, using artistic expression alongside cultural and historical analysis to illuminate the role of religion in modern Japanese society.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Chinese Religions
courses.description: Historical introduction to Chinese religions: Confucianism, Daoism, Buddhism, and folk religion.

source.text: RELI 288. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | ASIA 303 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Muhammad and the Qur'an
courses.description: An introduction to the life and significance of the Prophet Muhammad and the sacred scripture of Islam, the Qur'an. It offers discussion of textual sources for Muhammad's biography; his emulation and veneration in Muslim societies; and the nature, compilation, reception history, and range of interpretations of the Qur'an.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Special Topics in Religious Studies, FC-GLOBAL
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Memory and the Historical Jesus
courses.description: Who was Jesus? What did he teach? Can we interpret Jesus apart from religious frames or is our conception of Jesus always shaped by the religious texts preserving his memory? What modes of analysis and interpretation do contemporary historians apply to these texts, and what assumptions or biases can color their work? Comparing ancient and modern constructions of Jesus, this course probes the differences between cultural memory and historical writing as practices of knowing. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religious Frauds: Lies, Forgeries, and Fake News
courses.description: This course explores the problem of religious fraud-and more specifically, "pious fraud"-drawing case studies from Christian history. Although Christianity espouses a high moral code, some Christians have used deception to advance their beliefs and agendas: forging documents, inventing stories, and fabricating artifacts. Others have been suspected of these same activities. Throughout the semester, students wade through the thorny moral/ethical issues presented by the practice of pious fraud and debate possible cases. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Theories of Religion--Taboo and Transgression
courses.description: This course addresses terms such as "the sacred," "sacrifice," "the dead," "divinity," and "possession" to explore the limitations and new potentials of religious studies for describing human experience. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Social Theory and Cultural Diversity
courses.description: Introduction to basic thinking about cultural difference (race, gender, nationality, religion, etc.). The course encourages students to examine the ways paradigms shape how we act, think, and imagine as members of diverse cultures in the United States.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and the Human: Interrogating Individuality
courses.description: Notions of what a human being is--and what this means for how one should live--lie at the root of all religious traditions and also of secular ideologies. This course explores the ways that different religious and cultural communities have conceptualized human nature and how those understandings are reflected in personal identity and ways of organizing public life. Readings include historic and contemporary texts and case studies engaging Buddhism, Hinduism, and Christianity.

source.text: RELI 324. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion, Magic, and Science
courses.description: Critical exploration of the ways in which religion, magic, and science have been constructed as distinct domains of knowledge in the West since the late 19th century.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Protestant Tradition
courses.description: The course comes to provide students with historical and theological knowledge and conceptual tools that will enable them to understand the very rich and diverse Protestant tradition. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in American Law
courses.description: An exploration of the position of religion in American legal and social theory, with particular focus on jurisprudence under the First Amendment.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Liberal Tradition in American Religion
courses.description: An examination of the growth of liberal theological expressions, such as rationalism, romanticism, and modernism, from the early 18th century to the present.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in Modern Israel
courses.description: The relation between religious communities, their hopes and their agendas to the culture, politics, and law of the country has been a central feature of the Israeli state from its inception. Religious faiths, agendas, and affiliations have affected the character of the country, as well as its relationships with groups and governments around the globe.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Black Atlantic Religions
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Black Atlantic discourses from ethnographic and religious studies perspectives. Readings will privilege African-inspired performance and aesthetic forms as these are produced in religious practice. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islamic and Jewish Legal Systems
courses.description: In this course, on both Jewish and Islamic law, we will explore the nature, structure, development, and significance of the legal system of each of these two religions. Topics discussed include rituals, purity laws, commerce, warfare, and gender relations. There is no need to have any background in Hebrew or Arabic: all texts are provided in English, and no previous knowledge on Islam or Judaism is assumed.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Anthropology of Christianity
courses.description: This course introduces students to the anthropology of Christianity. Students will explore major themes of interest in the field. This course aims to familiarize students with the diversity of Christian religious experience and expression globally and to explore the mechanisms through which that diversity takes shape in various cultural contexts.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Mary in the Christian Tradition
courses.description: In certain eras, Mary has been more central to Catholic devotion than Christ. This course explores doctrine, liturgy, and popular devotion centering on the Virgin in medieval European Christianity, her impact on colonial religion in the New World, and her roles in Protestantism, Eastern Orthodoxy, and Islam. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Studies in Christian Theologies and Theologians
courses.description: An investigation of one writer or school in the history of Christian theology as an example of typical methods, positions, and problems within the tradition.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Medieval Religious Texts
courses.description: In this course students will read major medieval religious texts (Christian, Jewish, and/or Muslim), that permit close study of religious life, culture, and thought during the Middle Ages (broadly defined). The works will be in English translation, but students with appropriate linguistic knowledge may read the texts in their original language.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Art of Devotion in Medieval and Early Modern Europe
courses.description: This course examines creative expression at the service of religious belief from 1000 to 1700. Poetry, drama, art, architecture, and music will be the texts to understand the religious cultures of this rich period.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Race, Sexuality, and Disability in the History of Western Christianity
courses.description: Over time, Christian institutions and traditions have helped constitute contemporary narratives of race, sexuality, and disability in society. This course examines shifting definitions and specific case studies from the premodern era through to contemporary discourses and polemics in America. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 368. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER. | WGST 370 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Women Mystics
courses.description: An investigation of the forms, characteristics, and variety of the mystical experiences of women in medieval and modern Christianity, with comparative consideration of women mystics and spiritual leaders in at least two other religious traditions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Archaeology of Cult
courses.description: This course examines the archaeological context of Greek religion, cults, and associated rituals from the Bronze Age until the Classical period with emphasis on urban, rural, and panhellenic sanctuaries, and methods of approaching ancient religion and analyzing cult practices.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Story of Rama in India
courses.description: Explores Valmiki's Ramayana, alternate versions of the story, its performance in theater, and its role in politics. Students may not receive credit for both ASIA 332 / RELI 378 and ASIA/ RELI 382 .

source.text: RELI 378. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | ASIA 332 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Mahabharata: Remembered and Reimagined
courses.description: Explores Vyasa's Mahabharata as well as adaptations of the story in literature, theater, and film, with a focus on ethics and moral dilemmas in the story. Students may not receive credit for both ASIA 333 / RELI 379 and ASIA/ RELI 383 .

source.text: RELI 379. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | ASIA 333 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religions of South Asia
courses.description: Exploration of the major religious traditions of South Asia. Focuses on the beliefs and practices associated with different traditions, and the ways that these relate to one another and to broader political, historical, and cultural formations. Also addresses questions of modernization, reform, communal violence, and other transformations of religious life. Students will engage with a diverse array of sources, from epic literature and devotional poetry to visual art, architecture, and performance traditions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Story of Rama in Indian Culture--Experiential
courses.description: Explores Valmiki's Ramayana (story of the Hindu god Rama), alternate versions of the story, its performance in theater, and its role in politics. Students work outside of class to stage scenes from the Ramayana, open to the public. Students may not receive credit for both ASIA 332 / RELI 378 and ASIA/ RELI 382 .

source.text: RELI 382. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING, HI-PERFORM. | ASIA 382 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Mahabharata: Remembered and Reimagined--Experiential
courses.description: Introduction to the classical Mahabharata as well as modern retellings of the epic in contemporary literature, film, and theater of India. Students work outside class to stage one or more scenes from the Mahabharata, open to the public. Students may not receive credit for both ASIA 333 / RELI 379 and ASIA/ RELI 383 .

source.text: RELI 383. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | ASIA 383 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Globalization in Southeast Asia
courses.description: How does globalization affect religious life? How do historical, cultural, and religious traditions mediate the experience of globalization in particular locales? This course analyzes the forces and practices associated with political-economic and cultural globalization in Southeast Asia and explores the religious transformations and innovations that these processes have inspired.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Modern Muslims and the Qur'an
courses.description: This course introduces students to the multifaceted ways in which Muslims in the modern and contemporary periods have approached, experienced, and interpreted the Qur'an, including discussions of accessibility, hermeneutical methods, and exegetical themes.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Disciplining the Body and Mind: The Martial Arts of East Asia in Religion, History, and Culture
courses.description: This course offers an introduction to the history and practice of East Asian martial arts. We will explore the social, political, and cultural contexts of the martial arts, from the classical period to the present. Integral to this course is a practical component involving embodied experience with martial arts training.

source.text: RELI 387. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-KNOWING, HI-PERFORM. | ASIA 387 , COMM 387 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Gandhi - Politics, Principles, and the Person
courses.description: This course explores the ethical principles, civil and religious philosophies, and political life of Mohandas Gandhi, widely credited with leading India to independence from colonial rule through his politics of nonviolent resistance. The course focuses on key aspects of Gandhi's life and thought including his religious ideas, intellectual influences, responses to colonialism, theory and practice of nonviolence, critiques of caste and inequality, and insistence on Hindu-Muslim brotherhood. We will also examine his enduring impact on global and popular movements in India and internationally. Class material will include Gandhi's own writings, a set of secondary sources, and three Bollywood films.

courses.title: Topics in the Study of Religion
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Subject matter will vary with instructor but will always be focused on a particular problem or issue.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.description: This course is used for guided undergraduate research under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Religious Studies. Permission of the instructor is required.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 9 total completions.
