courses.title: Advanced Akkadian
courses.description: Readings in literary, epistolary, and juridical texts.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ugaritic
courses.description: Readings in the alphabetic texts of Ras Shamra and a study of the elements of Ugaritic grammar.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Biblical Coptic and Early Egyptian Monasticism
courses.description: Coptic, the last stage of Egyptian, a living language in the Roman and Byzantine period. Thorough grounding in the grammar of the Sahidic dialect as a basis for reading biblical monastic and Gnostic texts.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Syriac
courses.description: An introduction to the grammar of Classical Syriac for the purpose of reading Syriac Christian texts from late antiquity. Knowledge of another Semitic language (e.g., Hebrew, Arabic) would be an asset but is not required.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Teaching the Bible in Public Education
courses.description: This course explores the challenges, ethical questions, and opportunities inherent in teaching biblical literature within public educational settings--both secondary and higher-ed. It also equips students to make informed decisions on how to communicate critical academic ideas about the Bible in ways sensitive to students of different positionalities.

source.text: RELI 415. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Cult of Saints: Narratives, Materialities, Practices
courses.description: By late antiquity, the cult of martyrs and other saints had become "so popular among all levels of Christians, rich and poor, cleric and layperson, rustic and urban dweller, monastic and spouse," that it represented a "rudimentary framework for Christianity" (Limberis 2011). This course traces the origins and development of the cult, conceptualizing it as a network of discourses, practices, and representations. It also explores the cult's impact on neighboring, non-Christian cultures. Previously offered as RELI 614. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 416. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Post-Holocaust Ethics and Theology
courses.description: This course examines the challenges posed to ethics and theology by the Holocaust. We will address philosophical and moral issues such as the problem of evil, divine omniscience, omnipotence, suffering, theodicy, representation, testimony, and an ethics of memory. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 420. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | JWST 420 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Science
courses.description: This course explores the complex relation between religion and science in the modern world. Public disputes over teaching evolution in American schools serve as a central case study of this.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ethnicity, Race, and Religion in America
courses.description: A theoretical inquiry into ethnicity, race, and religion as constituents of personal and communal identity. Emphasis on global migrations, colonial and postcolonial relations, diasporic communities, and issues of religious pluralism.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Gender Theory and the Study of Religion
courses.description: An examination of contemporary gender theory, with particular focus on its application to the study of religion.

source.text: RELI 424. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | WGST 424 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Psychology of Religion
courses.description: A critical exploration of the concept of religious experience as defined by such authors as William James and Sigmund Freud. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Sacrifice of Abraham
courses.description: This course examines philosophical interpretations of the attempted sacrifice by Abraham of his beloved son, offering a comparative approach. The incident in Genesis is remarkably succinct for its controversial subject matter. We will compare this event with representations in Greek drama, the New Testament, and the Qur'an. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Spirit Possession and Mediumship
courses.description: This course explores the phenomenon of spirit possession and introduces students to various theoretical and methodological approaches to its academic study. In addition to critically engaging with accounts of spirit possession from around the world, students will explore various related themes of gender, power, and religious and cultural change. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Anthropology
courses.description: Religion studied anthropologically as a cultural, social, and psychological phenomenon in the works of classical and contemporary social thought. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Social Research in Religious Settings
courses.description: This advanced seminar investigates fundamental questions about religion's role in human societies through hands-on research. Students engage with classic and contemporary social theories about religion while designing and conducting research projects in local religious congregations. Through collaborative research, students develop social research skills while exploring how religion shapes individual lives and broader social dynamics. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Dimensions of Evil
courses.description: This course explores the meaning of evil. By investigating the moral dimensions of evil, its social uses, its figuration in cross-cultural religious texts, theology, folklore, and political imaginaries, this course develops a critical framework for understanding the diverse manifestations and varied cultural renderings of evil in the modern world. Previously offered as RELI 526.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: From Martin Luther to Martin Luther King Jr.: The Origins of Religious Freedom
courses.description: This course examines the theological and historical foundations of religious freedom in the United States, from the Protestant Reformation to the Civil Rights Movement. Starting with Martin Luther's challenge to the Catholic Church in "The Freedom of a Christian" (1520), the course traces key ideas such as religious tolerance, separation of church and state, and freedom of belief. Foundational documents from American democracy and the Civil Rights Movement will be used to explore how these concepts evolved and became central to American ideals of religious freedom. Readings and Discussions in English.

source.text: RELI 431. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES, FAD. | GERM 427 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Jesus Across Cultures
courses.description: This seminar examines Jesus as a divine, human, prophetic, and/or ethical figure across Catholic, Protestant, Muslim, and Buddhist communities globally in early, medieval, and Reformation eras, as well as in the modern and contemporary Americas. Specific attention will be paid to scientific, devotional, and media cultures which pose a variety of questions and methods for engagement with the theological and cultural questions that emerge from the earliest narratives of Jesus' life through to recent religious and moral movements.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion, Nature, and Environment
courses.description: A seminar on concepts of nature within religions and a variety of world-wide spiritual traditions. Emphasis on sacred space, place, and ritual as a vital intersection of religion and nature. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in Early America
courses.description: This course examines religion in America from precontact to the Civil War. We will chart the development of religious life, thought, and practice in North America, concentrating on areas later incorporated into the United States, but maintaining broad interest in other Americas. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: History of Religion in America since 1865
courses.description: An examination of primary sources in the history of American religion since the Civil War.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Evangelicalism in Contemporary America
courses.description: Juniors or seniors only. Examination of evangelicalism and its role in American society, politics, and culture. Exploration of its various subdivisions and its relation to such movements as fundamentalism, pentecostalism, revivalism, and premillennialism. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Contemporary Judaism
courses.description: The seminar examines the developments in gender roles and in sexuality in contemporary Judaism.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Asian Religions in America
courses.description: A study of intercultural interaction and interreligious encounter focusing on Asian religions in America, 1784 to the present.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Christian-Jewish Relations throughout the Ages
courses.description: An exploration of the varied and complex relationships which have developed between Christianity and Judaism, from the first century to the 21st century.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Native and Christian: Indigenous Engagements with Christianity
courses.description: This course examines diverse indigenous engagements with Christianity from earliest contacts to the present. Topics range from missionary contestations in colonial Mexico to the fight for religious freedom in 20th-century United States, from historical revitalization movements like the Ghost Dance to contemporary indigenous theologies in North and South America.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Sexuality in Jewish Tradition and History
courses.description: This course deals with various topics related to sexuality and marriage in Jewish tradition and history: sex outside of marriage, wedding ceremonies, regulations of marital sex, menstruation, homosexuality, and more.

source.text: RELI 450. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES. | WGST 450 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Documenting Religion
courses.description: This course examines the politics of representing religious difference. What happens when journalists, pollsters, filmmakers, or pundits attempt to describe, explain or decode religious communities they do not belong to? How do these efforts constitute cultural centers and margins? We examine the political and ethical problems inherent to representing religion. Topics might include documentary film, photojournalism, reality television, opinion polling, news media, and more.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Reformation
courses.description: Examines a movement of religious reform that shattered Latin Christendom and contributed many of the conditions of early modern Europe. Emphases: religious, political, social.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Monotheistic Mysticism
courses.description: In medieval Jewish Kabbalah, Christian mysticism, and Islamic Sufism, devotees attempt to express direct experiences of an infinite God. This course examines theories of mystical language, particularly the negation of language, the turn to the visual and the body, and the tension between communal and individual expressions of the divine.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Buddhist Meditation, Mindfulness, and Modernity
courses.description: This course introduces students to a variety of ancient and modern approaches to Buddhist meditation, to their philosophical underpinnings, and to the various claims and purposes associated with mindfulness practices in the past and today. Students will be expected to practice the different types of meditation discussed.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Modern Muslim Literatures
courses.description: Stresses the diversity of modern Islamic experience by examining the works of various Muslim authors. Genres may include travelogues, memoirs, novels, sermons, and treatises, among others.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion, Fundamentalism, and Nationalism
courses.description: An exploration of explosive combinations of religion and politics in the Iranian revolution, the Palestinian movement, Hindu nationalism in India, and Christian fundamentalism in America.

source.text: RELI 481. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-VALUES. | PWAD 481 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Sex, Gender, and Religion in South Asia
courses.description: This seminar draws on feminist and philosophical theory, including the works of Plato, Butler, and Foucault, as well as postcolonial theory, to explore the categories of sex and gender in South Asian religions. We also analyze the moral cultivation of the self in relation to gender identity in South Asia.

source.text: RELI 482. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | ASIA 482 , WGST 482 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Islam
courses.description: This course approaches constructions of gender and sexuality in Muslim societies in diverse historical and geographical contexts. It focuses on changing interpretations of gender roles and sexual norms. Themes include gender in Islamic law, sexual ethics, masculinity, homosexuality, marriage, and dress.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islam and Feminism/Islamic Feminism
courses.description: This course explores Muslim women scholars, activists, and movements that have, over the course of the past 150 years, participated in the debate about the compatibility and relationship of Islam and feminism. It offers an introduction to feminist debates about religion and patriarchy focusing on Islam as 'other' and juxtaposes it critical analysis of contextual expressions of Muslim and Islamic feminist activists, thinkers, and movements that challenge and change gender norms and practices.

source.text: RELI 486. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ASIA 486 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Mountains, Pilgrimage, and Sacred Places in Japan
courses.description: This course explores the role that mountains and pilgrimage have played in Japanese cosmology and how they relate to methodology of studying place and space.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Shinto in Japanese History
courses.description: This course discusses the development of Shinto in Japanese history and covers themes such as myths, syncretism, sacred sites, iconography, nativism, religion and the state, and historiography.

source.text: RELI 488. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | ASIA 488 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Animals in Japanese Religion
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course examines the cultural construction of animals in Japanese myth, folklore, and religion.

source.text: RELI 489. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-KNOWING. | ASIA 489 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The History of the Bible in Modern Study
courses.description: This course will examine how the modern historical-critical enterprise of biblical scholarship arose, out of what historical circumstances, for what purposes, and to what effect. What are its major aspects? How does it relate to other forms of academic and theological inquiry? How has this enterprise fared in recent times?

source.text: RELI 501. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Myths and Epics of the Ancient Near East
courses.description: An examination of Babylonian, Canaanite, Egyptian, Hittite, and Sumerian texts from the prebiblical era, focusing on representative myths, epics, sagas, songs, proverbs, prophecies, and hymns. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 502. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | FOLK 502 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Exploring the Dead Sea Scrolls
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to the Dead Sea Scrolls and the different Jewish groups connected with them. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 503. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH. | JWST 503 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Readings in Hebrew Bible
courses.description: This course will examine a major corpus of the Hebrew Bible with attention to the full range of historical-critical issues. Attention will be paid as well to early forms of biblical interpretation and their use in the religious life of subsequent communities.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ancient Synagogues
courses.description: This is a course on ancient synagogues in Palestine and the Diaspora from the Second Temple period to the seventh century CE.

source.text: RELI 512. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | CLAR 512 , JWST 512 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Judaism and the Search for Christian Origins
courses.description: Although the origins of Christianity clearly lie in Judaism--the religious framework inherited by Jesus and his disciples--scholars disagree over how and when the two traditions diverged. This course explores critical issues in the conceptualization of this parting, including the theoretical difficulty of distinguishing religion from ethnicity in a premodern context, competing ways of analyzing intermediate groups ("Jewish Christianities"), and the methodological and ethical problems of 19th-20th century scholarship in this area (e.g., Protestant bias, antisemitism).

source.text: RELI 514. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Cultural Histories of the New Testament
courses.description: This course traces the "lives" of individual New Testament texts to illuminate the shifting interests of Christians through different periods. Topics include the Gospel of Mark, the Gospel of John, the letters of Paul and his imitators, and the book of Revelation. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

source.text: RELI 515. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: 19th-Century Critiques of Religion
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An exploration of influential 19th-century critiques of religion, including texts by such thinkers as Feuerbach, Marx, Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Stanton, Douglass, and Freud.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ethnographic Approaches to Contemporary Religion
courses.description: Critical exploration of exemplary contemporary ethnographies of religion focusing on the ways that ethnographic methods and writing styles shape knowledge of religious and cultural life in various traditions and parts of the world. Topics considered include field work, culture, ethics, and the challenges of interpreting and representing religious experience.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Seminar in Religion and Literature
courses.description: Seminar topic varies.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religious Metaphor and Symbol
courses.description: This course explores the myriad and complex issues related to the function of metaphor and symbol in religious language.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Rituals and Rhetorics of Religion
courses.description: An examination of ritual, allegory, and symbol as modes of religious expression in cultic and literary contexts.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Genealogies of Religion
courses.description: This seminar explores the historical development of "religion" as a concept and object of academic scholarship through the critical study of key texts and foundational debates about religion in Western thought.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Women, Gender, and Judaism
courses.description: This course examines historical developments in the study of women and gender in Judaism. We will discuss efforts to challenge and revitalize Jewish tradition through the lens of gender theory and other critical interpretive approaches. Topics to be addressed include biblical interpretation, Jewish law, feminist Jewish theology and liturgy, the renewal of ritual, the rabbinic ordination of women, gender identity, race, sexuality, queer, trans, and non-binary approaches, and representations of these themes in various media.

source.text: RELI 533. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | JWST 533 , WGST 533 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Mormonism and the American Experience
courses.description: Exploration of the history, beliefs, and practices of Mormons. Will include visits to Latter-Day Saints services, guest speakers, and discussion of race and gender in the contemporary church.

source.text: RELI 540. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, RELI 140 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Evangelicalism from a Global Perspective
courses.description: The course will examine the evangelical tradition from a global perspective, exploring the tradition from its early rise in Europe to its impact on the Americas, Africa, and Asia. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and the Counterculture
courses.description: The course examines the interaction between the values and messages of the counterculture and religious groups, ideas, and practices during the Vietnam War era. It also investigates the impact of countercultural norms and styles on the current American religious scene. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion, Race, and Inquisition in the Spanish Empire
courses.description: This course on the "Atlantic World" studies Muslims, Christians, and Jews in the medieval Iberian kingdoms, then the religious "other" in the colonial expansion to Latin America, by deploying theories concerning race, gender, sexuality, and postcoloniality.

source.text: RELI 564. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | HIST 564 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Medieval Jews and the Bible
courses.description: This course explores the Jewish interpretation of the Bible, focusing on important commentaries from influential medieval Ashkenazi and Sephardic thinkers.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islamic and Jewish Legal Literature
courses.description: This course explores many aspects of the Halakhah, the Jewish traditional legal system, focusing on issues such as rituals, holidays, religious obligations and prohibitions, and laws regulating sexual activity.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Interfaith Marriages and Intimacy in World Religions
courses.description: This seminar explores the topic of intimate relations between people who consider themselves, or are considered by others, to be part of different religious groups. We will explore cases in which such relations achieve the social sanction of marriage and cases in which the relations are of a more temporary nature.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islam & the Black Global South
courses.description: This course is a thematic and historical exploration of Black Muslim communities and movements in the United States and beyond. It also investigates the political solidarities, economic and social relationships, and religious connections between Black communities across the US, Europe, Caribbean, South America and Africa.

source.text: RELI 580. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Sufism
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A survey of Islamic mysticism, its sources in the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad, and its literary, cultural, and social deployment in Arab, Persian, Indic, and Turkish regions.

source.text: RELI 581. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | ASIA 581 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islam and Islamic Art in South Asia
courses.description: A survey of the formation of Islamic traditions in the subcontinent from the eighth century to the present, with emphasis on religion and politics, the role of Sufism, types of popular religion, and questions of Islamic identity.

source.text: RELI 582. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | ASIA 582 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Culture in Iran, 1500-Present
courses.description: Iran from the rise of the Safavid empire to the Islamic Republic. Topics include Shi'ism, politics, intellectual and sectarian movements, encounters with colonialism, art and architecture, music, literature.

source.text: RELI 583. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | ASIA 583 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Qur'an as Literature
courses.description: A nontheological approach to the Qur'an as a literary text, emphasizing its history, form, style, and interpretation.

source.text: RELI 584. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | ASIA 584 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Culture of Turkey
courses.description: This course will cover the history of Turkey from the Byzantine period until contemporary times. Key aspects of Turkish culture (architecture, music, poetry to arts) will be covered.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Women and Gender in Japanese Religions
courses.description: This seminar explores the roles of women in the religions of Japan (including Buddhism, Shinto, folk religions, pilgrimage, new religions movements, and new spirituality culture) from goddesses, shamans, nuns, and pilgrims to demons, temptresses, and lesser human beings. The course traces these themes across Japanese socioeconomic and religious history.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islam and Sexual Diversity
courses.description: This course explores sexual norms and practices in Muslim contexts in the premodern and modern periods. It considers theories from sexuality, gender, and queer studies, and focuses on the contextual production of sexual norms, going beyond the sex and gender binary, and reflecting on a diverse range of sexual practices in Muslim communities and societies, analyzing concepts such as power, pleasure, control, as they are mapped onto and lived in diverse Muslim bodies.

source.text: RELI 587. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | ASIA 587 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Food in East Asia
courses.description: This course examines how religious food practices have developed over time in East Asia. By exploring the historical roots and transnational spread of these traditions, we will analyze how religious communities have preserved, transformed, and adapted their foodways over time. Honors version available.

source.text: RELI 588. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | ASIA 588 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Topics in the Study of Religion
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Subject matter will vary with instructor but will always be focused on a particular problem or issue.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religious Conflict and Literature in India
courses.description: Historical causes of violence between Hindus and Muslims in modern India. Short stories, poetry, and novels in translation are used to explore how conflicts over religious sites, religious conversion, image worship, and language contributed to a sense of conflicting religious identity.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: What Is Scripture? Formations of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament Canon
courses.description: The course traces the past and continued canonical processes that define what the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament has been and is today, with a focus on the history of biblical interpretation.

source.text: RELI 602. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | JWST 602 .

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Bible and the History of the Self
courses.description: This course explores changing conceptions of the self and its relationship to society through the lens of biblical interpretation. How do contemporary notions of the self impact our understanding of the Hebrew Bible? What alternatives to the modern self are available in the Bible? What does the history of biblical interpretation have to tell us about the history of the self? The course focuses on close analysis of biblical texts, translation, and the history of Western thought.

source.text: RELI 603. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH. | JWST 603 .

courses.title: Problems in Early Christian Literature and History
courses.description: Honors version available.

courses.title: The Messiah and the Apocalypse
courses.description: Ideas concerning the Messiah and the end of the world held by Jews, Christians, and Muslims. Emphasis on the beginning of the Christian era.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Christianity and Greco-Roman Culture
courses.description: The seminar surveys the development of Christianity in the Roman empire and examines a variety of attitudes adopted by early Christians toward Greco-Roman philosophy, religion, education, and literature.

courses.title: Readings in the Apostolic Fathers
courses.description: Reading of the Apostolic Fathers. Students must have completed two courses in New Testament/Early Christianity and two years of Greek.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Death and Afterlife in the Ancient World
courses.description: Examinations of practices and discourses pertaining to death and the afterlife in the ancient civilizations of Near East, Greece, and Rome. Honors version available.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Feminism and Religion
courses.description: This course introduces students to the rich and multi-faceted debates within and about feminism and religion. Through the cultivation of careful and critical reading practice of primary texts by religious feminists and their secular critics, the course enables students to recognize the patterns and arguments of historical and contemporary debates within and across religious traditions and communities, while continuously tracing the ethical commitments and underlying values of feminist scholars and activists.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Contemporary Catholicism
courses.description: This advanced seminar is for undergraduate and graduate students who have at least a basic knowledge about Catholicism. The range of topics to be discussed is open and will depend on students' interests and suggestions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Body and Suffering in Christian Mysticism
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Medieval Christians consistently focused on the suffering body as a means of reflecting on Christ's sacrifice. This course considers how medical theories of cognition, gender, and pain influenced the potential role of the body in medieval mystical experience.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Readings in Islamicate Literatures
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Study of selected religious, literary, and historical texts in Arabic, Persian, or Urdu.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Observation and Interpretation of Religious Action
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Exercises (including field work) in learning to read the primary modes of public action in religious traditions, e.g., sermons, testimonies, rituals, and prayers.

courses.title: Honors in Religious Studies
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Required of all students reading for honors in religious studies.

courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Required of all students reading for honors in religious studies.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Advanced undergraduate or graduate standing and permission of the instructor. Subject matter should be arranged with a specific instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Capstone: Undergraduate Seminar
courses.description: Majors only. Concentrating on a different theme each year, this departmental seminar introduces the different areas and approaches in religious studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Theory and Method in the Study of Religion
courses.description: Graduate standing in religious studies or permission of the instructor. A basic problems and methods course required of all graduate students in religious studies.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Literature of Israel
courses.description: A study of the religious traditions in ancient Israelite literature from the 12th through the second centuries BCE.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Critical Approaches to the Study of the Hebrew Bible and its History of Interpretation
courses.description: Exploration of current critical approaches to the study of the Hebrew Bible, including those oriented toward a study of its interpretive history.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Readings in Religions of the Ancient Near East
courses.description: Focusing on the Mediterranean religions before Alexander, the course consists of readings of original documents in translation, illustrating theology and cult, as well as on the major history of religions interpretations.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Early Christian History and Literature
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A critical study of the history and literature of early Christianity from Paul to Irenaeus, with texts to be read in the original languages.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Early Jewish History and Literature
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An examination of the main varieties of pre-rabbinic Judaism: Hellenistic Judaism, apocalyptic Judaism, and the Judaism of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Eastern Christianities: Historical, Cultural, and Postcolonial Perspectives
courses.description: This course explore the identities, histories, social organization, and practices of the world's ''Eastern'' and ''Orthodox'' Christians.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Readings in Greco-Roman Religion
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Opportunity for reading of ancient documents representing the more important religious trends of the Greco-Roman world.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Critical and Comparative Lineages in Religion and Culture
courses.description: Exploration of intellectual lineages shaping the contemporary study of religion and culture.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Theories of Religion and Culture
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Studies in early modern, Enlightenment and Romantic political, philosophical, and literary texts.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Critical Approaches to Religion and Culture
courses.description: Graduate standing in religious studies or permission of the instructor. Exploration of various forms of contemporary critical thought (including gender theory, critical race theory, and postcolonial studies) in order to assess the value of these critical tools for the study of religion.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ethnographic Research Methods: Ethnography of Religion and Religious Formations
courses.description: This course engages the practices, politics, ethics, and epistemology of ethnography as a technique of data production, analysis, and representation. While we will privilege issues and themes related to the study of religion, the course offers a broad, multidisciplinary approach to the construction and execution of ethnographic research.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Modernity
courses.description: Graduate standing in religious studies or permission of the instructor. This course examines the relationships between religion and modernity, both as conceptual categories and through ethnographic studies of religion and/in modern life.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Studies in the Rhetoric of Images
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Selected readings on image production, exhibition, and interpretation, with consideration of different ritual and cultic settings.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Critical Works in Religion and Literature
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Textual analysis of several theoretical and literary works dealing with selected problems in religion and literature.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Approaches to the Study of Religion in the Americas
courses.description: Explores methods, theories, and genealogies that shape the study of religion in the Americas. The course introduces students to key historiographical contexts and theoretical debates that will help them situate the field within the discipline of Religious Studies.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Themes in African American Religious History
courses.description: Graduate standing in religious studies or permission of the instructor. A historical and thematic survey of the religions of African Americans from the precolonial era to the present.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Literature in America
courses.description: Graduate standing in religious studies or permission of the instructor. A study of the religious tradition in American literature from the Puritan period to the present.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Current Trends in American Judaism
courses.description: The course aims at examining the current developments in American Judaism: cultural, spiritual, liturgical, as well as social and institutional.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in Colonial Americas
courses.description: A study of religion in the Americas from pre-contact indigenous communities to 19th century wars of independence. The course examines cases of migration, encounter, rebellion, and institutionalization across the continent and introduces theoretical debates about colonialism, hybridity, revival, and revolution.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion in Postcolonial Americas
courses.description: A study of religion in the Americas through the lens of post-colonialism understood as a concept, a method, and an historical period. This course introduces students to theoretical debates about power, culture, history, and representation to better understand the present and future of the field.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Christian-Jewish Encounter in America
courses.description: Course examines the Christian-Jewish encounter in America from the 17th century to the present. Analyzes both theological and social interactions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Approaches to Medieval and Early Modern Studies
courses.description: Graduate standing in religious studies or permission of the instructor. An introduction to the problems and methods in the study of medieval and early modern religion in the West.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Approaches to Islamic Studies
courses.description: An introduction to the academic study of Islam and Muslims, including the history of the field, theory and method in Islamic studies, pedagogy, and important subfields. Gateway course.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islam and Reform
courses.description: Exploration of reformist intellectual movements in modern Muslim societies, paying close attention to the case of post-revolutionary Iran and examining the compatibility of Islam and human rights, women's rights, democracy, and fresh hermeneutical approaches to scriptures.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Critical Genealogies of Middle East Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This seminar is the core course for the graduate certificate in Middle East studies. It is an introduction to critical issues in the study of the Middle East, focusing on classic works of the humanities and social sciences.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Seminar in Biblical Studies
courses.description: Topics vary; consult the department.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Advanced Hebrew Readings
courses.description: Required preparation, proficiency in Hebrew. Primary readings in portions of the Hebrew Bible (e.g., Pentateuch, Deuteronomistic History, prophetic texts, Psalms) or in non-biblical texts (pre-exilic inscriptions, Dead Sea Scrolls) with attention to issues of interpretation.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ancient Israelite Religion
courses.description: Explores the field of ancient Israelite religion as it has been conceived in contemporary scholarship. We will review the relevant textual and archaeological data, acquaint ourselves with current debates, and examine the different approaches that scholars have adopted to the problem of ancient Israelite religion.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Historical Hebrew and Semitic Linguistics
courses.description: An introduction to the historical development of ancient Hebrew within a comparative Semitic framework, with attention to the full range of relevant textual evidence (e.g., biblical Hebrew, pre-exilic inscriptions, Dead Sea Scrolls).

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Hellenistic Religious Texts in Greek
courses.description: Studies in Greek texts drawn from early Christianity, Judaism, and other religions of the Greco-Roman World.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Apostolic Fathers
courses.description: Required preparation, proficiency in Greek. Permission of the instructor. A study of selected works of the Apostolic Fathers, including Barnabas, Ignatius, and Polycarp.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Textual Criticism of the Greek Bible
courses.description: Required preparation, proficiency in Greek. Permission of the instructor. Reconstruction; application of text-critical principles.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Readings in Early Jewish and Christian Apocalyptic
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Readings from apocalyptic texts in the original languages.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Diaspora Judaism
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. Seminar examines the evidence for the ancient Jewish communities of Egypt, Rome, Asia Minor, and Mesopotamia.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Readings in Talmud
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An introduction to the study of the Babylonian Talmud in the original Hebrew and Aramaic, with the traditional commentaries. The emphasis is on understanding Talmudic logic.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Problems in Rabbinic Historiography
courses.description: Examination of the methodological problems of using rabbinic materials as sources for the history of Judaism in the period after 70 CE.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ancient Rhetoric and Early Christianity
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Survey of the development of rhetorical theory and practice through the Hellenistic and Roman Period. Explores the connection between rhetorical tradition and early Christian literature.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Gnostic Scriptures
courses.description: Close reading and interpretation of ancient Gnostic texts found near Nag Hammadi in Egypt.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Ancient Philosophy and Early Christianity
courses.description: Required preparation, proficiency in Greek and/or Latin. Survey of the Hellenistic schools of philosophy and their impact on early Christian theories of the universe, ethics, cultural history, and salvation.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Seminar in Religion and Culture
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topics vary; consult the department.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Postcolonial Approaches to the Study of Religion
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An examination of major themes in contemporary postcolonial thought, and the application of this work to the study of religion.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Body, Materiality, History
courses.description: This course addresses theories of the body in the study of history. It expands standard notions of "the body" by considering developments in scientific and medical approaches, then turning to the fields of gender and sexuality studies, disability studies, critical race theory, and postcolonial theory, and ending with consideration of the body's expression through material culture. Extensive historical case studies will be taken from scholarship on Western, Eastern, and indigenous religions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Space, Place, and Religion
courses.description: This interdisciplinary graduate seminar focuses on religion, space, and place in the United States.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Topics in Religion and Law
courses.description: This course examines selected themes in legal and social theory relating to the position of religion in contemporary American society.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Seminar in American Religion
courses.description: Topics vary. May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Social Issues in America
courses.description: Historical analysis of the relationship between religious developments and social issues in America. Topics may include economics, politics, and social reform.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religion and Cultural Contact in America
courses.description: Examination of religion in America through instances of intercultural contact. Topics vary.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Roman Catholicism in America
courses.description: A seminar on Roman Catholicism in the United States that also considers developments elsewhere in the Western hemisphere. Focus is on ritual practice and visual culture.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Medieval Religious Texts
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Selected texts which illumine significant aspects of medieval religious culture are read in the original languages.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Texts of the Catholic and Protestant Reformations
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Selected texts which illumine significant aspects of the Catholic and Protestant Reformations are read in the original languages.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Methods and Topics in the Study of Western Religious Traditions
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Exploration of one enduring issue in the history of the Western Christian tradition. The instructor selects several case studies that illustrate both the topic and the developments within traditions.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Islamic Thought
courses.description: Required preparation, proficiency in Arabic and/or Persian. Advanced study of major Islamic thinkers and topics, based on original language texts and modern scholarly interpretations.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: The Study of Asian Religions and the Construction of the Field
courses.description: Introduction to major approaches and methodological questions in the study of Asian religions. This course serves as a gateway course.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Topics in the Study of Religion
courses.description: Graduate standing in religious studies or permission of the instructor. Topics vary.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Religious Studies Professional Development Seminar
courses.description: This course seeks to prepare students for professional academic careers in Religious Studies and cognate disciplines by focusing on the skills and practices associated with success in research, publishing, and the job market.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Practices of Professional Development
courses.description: This course prepares doctoral students for careers in Religious Studies and cognate disciplines by focusing on the skills and practices associated with success in research, publishing and the job market. Focuses on skills development and strategies including conceptualizing and cultivating a professional persona, planning and presenting research, publishing, alt-ac career options, the academic job search, and professional ethics. Includes practical work as well as discussion.
